title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: L is a family of subsets of a set, with |L| = the union of its members. For x in |L|, write L_x = {A in L : x in A}. Write A° for the set of x in A such that A is minimal in L_x (the 'open stratum' of A). L' denotes the members with A° nonempty.

The previous page proves three conditions equivalent:
1°) Every L_x has a smallest element A(x).
2°) Two conditions hold:
  α) A∩B is the union of the C in L with C ⊂ A and C ⊂ B;
  β) every L_x has a minimal element.
3°) Three conditions hold:
  γ) |L| is the disjoint union of the A°, A in L';
  δ) every A is the union of the B° contained in it;
  η) x in A° and x in B imply A ⊂ B.

This page contains two remarks and a definition.

Remark 1 (the image reads 'β) du 2°'): β is automatic if L is finite. More generally it is automatic if L is artinian for inclusion, i.e. has no infinite strictly decreasing chain A1 ⊃ A2 ⊃ ..., since then minimal elements exist. Counterexample otherwise: take L to be the terms of such a chain with nonempty intersection. Then α holds, because intersections are members of L. But β fails at points of the intersection of the A_i.

Remark 2: 'In 3°), δ) n'est pas ...' (probably 'superflu' or 'conséquence'). Grothendieck tries to support this with an example: L = {A,B,C,D} on points x,y,z,t, with A∩C = D and A∪C ⊂ B. Then D° = D, A° = A∖D, C° = C∖D, B° = B∖(A∪C). The example is entirely struck out; he notes 'A° ⊂ B but also A ⊂ B', so it does not separate the conditions. A margin cross-reference to chapter VIII, pp. 44–45 is also struck.

Definition: L is pre-admissible if it satisfies the equivalent conditions 1°–3°. It is admissible if moreover every A° is nonempty, i.e. L' = L. This is completed on the next page. A margin query asks whether one should also require every A in L to be nonempty.

Purpose: this sets up the next page's dictionary. Admissible families correspond to a poset I, a set S and a surjection S → I. Equivalently, they are stratified sets over a poset with its Alexandrov topology, the members of L being the closed strata. This is a combinatorial foundation for the 'algèbre des figures'.
errors: If the uncrossed Remark 2 claims δ) is independent of the other conditions in 3°), that claim is false under the definitions of the previous page. A° ⊂ A by definition. Given x in A, γ gives a B with x in B°. Then η gives B ⊂ A, hence B° ⊂ A. So δ follows from γ and η, which likely explains why the counterexample was abandoned and struck out.
Likewise, in the previous page's proof of 3° ⇒ 1°, the appeal to δ is unnecessary: η alone gives A ⊂ B.
The attempted example (A∩C = D, A∪C ⊂ B) is not a counterexample to anything, as Grothendieck himself notes before crossing it out.

ideas.what: Smallest-member condition for a family of subsets, and its equivalence with intersection-closure up to unions plus existence of minimal elements; the artinian hypothesis making the latter automatic
ideas.modern_name: Minimal open neighbourhoods / Alexandrov (finitely generated) topology; descending chain condition

ideas.what: Decomposition of |L| into disjoint 'open strata' A° indexed by L', with each A a union of strata
ideas.modern_name: Stratification over a poset (closed strata = closures of fibres of a map S → I)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; formalised as poset-stratified spaces by MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratified spaces informally; this combinatorial formulation is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Definition of pre-admissible and admissible families (admissible = all strata nonempty)
ideas.modern_name: Set stratified by a poset with nonempty strata (surjective stratification map)

deep.surprise_reason: This is elementary order-theoretic bookkeeping: an artinian remark, a failed independence example and a definition. It sets up the stratified-poset dictionary of the next page, which is itself standard (Alexandrov topology). Its only interest is as a draft of the foundations of the 'algèbre des figures'.
